newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electric futures hold gains after new highs.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electric futures hold gains after new highs.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures settled higher Thursday, holding on to early gains after posting new life-of-contract highs on continued strength in the physical power market in the West.
Very warm weather in parts of California and triple-digit readings in the interior section of the Southwest propelled spot power values again in the West.

Firm, peak power prices at the California-Oregon Border (COB) for Friday firmed to $22.00-25.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) from Wednesday's $19.00-21.00, while those at the Palo Verde (PV) switchyard near Phoenix, Arizona, rallied to $39.00-43.00 from $29.00-35.00 yesterday.
But a decline in natural gas futures weighed down the electricity complex from its early highs, market sources said.
The NYMEX June Henry Hub contract finished 8.1 cents at $2.195 per million British thermal units after falling to a session low of $2.175.
Traders said power futures also eased when concerns faded over an explosion at a storage facility operated by the U.S. Department of Energy in Washington state.
The Hanford facility is located near the 1,158 megawatt (MW) WNP-2 nuclear power plant in Richland, Wash.
The nuclear plant, which has been shut late March, was reportedly unaffected by the blast.
June COB futures settled up eight cents at 18.18 a MWh after posting a new contract high at $18.50.
July COB finished five cents to $19.20 after hitting a new high at $19.50. Other COB months ended flat to 32 cents higher.
June PV futures settled up 11 cents at $24.26, off from an early new contract high at $24.70.
July PV finished up 20 cents at $26.50 after posting a contract high at $27.00. Deferred PV contracts ended down six to up 40 cents.
Despite weakness in natgas futures, heat in the Southwest and ongoing rise in physical prices would lend support to power futures, market sources said.
"It's still pretty solid," said an East Coast futures trader.
"I would give it more room on downside, but prescheduled prices are so strong, prices will probably stay up," said a Northwest futures trader.
In the Northwest, temperatures are expected to average six to 12 degrees F above normal through Saturday and drop to one to five degrees below normal Sunday.
In the Southwest, readings would run six to 12 degrees F above normal, while coastal areas would remain one to five degrees F above normal.
NYMEX estimated 695 COB and 820 PV contracts were sold, up from yesterday's 227 COB and 700 PV lots.
